title: Every gtkx subcommand silently accepts unknown options, so a misspelled option yields a wrong artifact or a silent no-op with exit 0
why: Ruled out as a missing feature rather than a broken one, and as third-party parser default behavior that no GTKX code path contradicts.

title: The string codec accepts null and undefined for a non-nullable `const gchar *` parameter and passes NULL to C, aborting the process on the resulting GLib assertion
why: Ruled out on two of the listed grounds: (a) the reproduction misuses the API in a way GTKX's own documented contract forbids, and (b) what is missing is a feature (runtime nullability metadata) that the descriptor model has never had, not a codec that is broken.

title: The integer, float and enum codecs silently coerce null and undefined to 0 instead of rejecting them

title: Held keyboard modifiers never reach userEvent.click, so ctrl-click and shift-click are indistinguishable from a plain click
why: Reproduced 3/3 failures, then ruled the report out on two independent grounds.

title: GObject.disconnect() with a handler id that is no longer connected emits a GLib critical and aborts the process instead of throwing
why: Ruled out on three of the listed grounds: the GLib C API documents this behavior, the reproduction uses the raw API where GTKX documents and ships a guarded one, and what is being asked for is an added guard on a 1:1 binding rather than a broken function.

title: An application whose last window is closed or unmounted never exits, and the surviving invisible process makes every later launch of the same application exit silently with status 0
why: Ruled out on three of the listed grounds: the GLib/GTK4 documentation says this is what happens outside `g_application_run()`, the GTKX documentation prescribes the explicit path the repro departs from, and the auto-quit was never implemented (a missing feature, not a broken one).

title: GLib timeouts, idles and promisified GIO calls never run when no application element is mounted: the process exits 0 immediately and the awaited promise never settles
why: Ruled out on two grounds: the GLib C API documents this exact behavior, and the part that is not GLib semantics is a convenience GTKX never claimed, not a broken path.
